claims.nodeLabel: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)
claims.sourceText: Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense FOIA release, case 97-F-1677, September 1997
claims.text: DoD records released under FOIA case 97-F-1677 describe numerous unidentified craft over Malmstrom AFB, Montana, in November 1975, and show that they could not be intercepted by multiple F-106 fighters.

claims.sourceText: Halt memorandum, 'Unexplained Lights,' 13 Jan 81, released under DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677
claims.text: Halt's memo states the object was 'metalic in appearance and triangular in shape, approximately two to three meters across the base and approximately two meters high,' and that it 'illuminated the entire forest with a white light.'

claims.sourceText: Halt memorandum, 13 Jan 81, released under DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677
claims.text: The memo's closing sentence reads: 'Numerous individuals, including the undersigned, witnessed the activities in paragraphs 2 and 3.' It is signed CHARLES I. HALT, Lt Col, USAF, Deputy Base Commander.

a.label: 1975 SAC Nuclear-Base Overflights (Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot)

edges.label: Occurred six years after the Air Force closed Blue Book on a no-threat finding
edges.note: The USAF fact sheet states Blue Book was terminated on 17 December 1969 on the conclusion that no UFO had ever indicated a threat to national security. The 1975 records document unidentified objects over nuclear weapons installations.

edges.label: Halt authored and signed the 'Unexplained Lights' memorandum
edges.note: Halt was Deputy Base Commander of the 81st Combat Support Group and signed the memo on 13 Jan 81. The document is his; his authorship has never been disputed by the Air Force.

edges.label: Halt personally led the 28 December 1980 forest patrol
edges.note: Halt's own memo states 'Numerous individuals, including the undersigned, witnessed the activities in paragraphs 2 and 3.'

edges.label: Released to The Black Vault under DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677
edges.note: The Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense, Freedom of Information and Security Review Office released the memo in September 1997 under case 97-F-1677.

edges.label: The memo is the primary official record of the incident
edges.note: The memo is the only contemporaneous US government document describing the events; everything else in the case is witness statement or later recollection.

edges.note: A congressionally directed review of the historical record omits the best-documented physical-trace incident at a NATO nuclear-capable base, for which the Pentagon's own FOIA office has released the commander's memorandum.
